title: Senior's toolkit: scripts that survive review
summary: Strict mode, shellcheck, bash -x, trap with mktemp, safe expansions, read -r, here-docs and timeout.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: scripts that survive review
steps.body: A deploy script runs unattended with real credentials. These are the habits a reviewer looks for first, because each one prevents a known kind of outage.

toolkit.what: Stops the script at the first failing command, on unset variables, and when any part of a pipeline fails.
flags: an unset variable is an error, not an empty string
a pipeline fails if any stage fails, not only the last

toolkit.what: A linter for shell scripts. Catches missing quotes, unsafe `rm`, broken tests and many silent bugs. Run it in CI.
flags: silence one rule on the next line, with a reason

toolkit.what: Prints each command after expansion before running it. Shows exactly which value a variable had when it failed.
flags: trace only one part of the script
add line numbers to the trace

toolkit.what: Runs cleanup however the script ends: success, error or Ctrl+C. Pair it with `mktemp` for temporary files.
Parameter expansions that fail loudly on a missing value, or fall back to a default.
flags: stop with `msg` if VAR is unset or empty
use `x` if VAR is unset or empty

toolkit.cmd: while IFS= read -r line; do ...; done < <file>
toolkit.what: Reads a file line by line without mangling spaces or backslashes. `for line in $(cat file)` splits on every space.
toolkit.example: while IFS= read -r host; do ssh "$host" uptime; done < hosts.txt

toolkit.what: A here-doc: writes a multi-line block. Quoting `'EOF'` stops `$` and backticks from being expanded inside.
Kills a command that runs too long, so one hung `curl` or `ssh` does not stall the whole pipeline.
flags: send SIGKILL 5 s after the first signal if it is still alive

steps.prompt: A cleanup script ran `rm -rf "$DEPLOY_DIR"/*` on a new server and deleted everything under `/`. Nothing else changed. What would have prevented it?
options: `set -u` or `"${DEPLOY_DIR:?}"`: the variable was unset, so the path became `/*`
steps.explain: An unset variable expands to an empty string, so `"$DEPLOY_DIR"/*` became `/*`. `set -u` stops the script at the first unset variable, and `${DEPLOY_DIR:?}` refuses an empty one too. shellcheck warns about this exact line (SC2115).

steps.prompt: Match each line to what it does.
pairs: `curl ... | tar xz` fails if curl fails
stop the script when TOKEN is empty
delete the temp folder however the script ends
give up on a host that hangs

steps.prompt: Complete the strict-mode line at the top of a script.
steps.explain: `-e` exit on error, `-u` no unset variables, `-o pipefail` take the first failure in a pipeline. `-x` (trace) is for debugging, not for every run.
`:-` uses the default when the variable is unset **or empty**. `${PORT-8080}` (without the colon) would print an empty line, because PORT is set.

steps.prompt: Put the top of a safe download script in order.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Start every script with the shebang and `set -euo pipefail`, run `shellcheck` before you ask for review, and wrap every network call in `timeout`. When a script misbehaves in CI, rerun it with `bash -x` instead of adding echo lines.
